key_insight: Incorporating explicit multi-step reasoning into 3D visual grounding pipelines enables models to resolve complex, relational referring expressions much more effectively than standard fusion-only approaches.
problem_solved: Overcomes the limited reasoning ability of current 3D visual grounding models that fail on relational, compositional, or context-dependent referring queries in cluttered 3D scenes.
method: Augment a 3D-text fusion architecture with a dedicated reasoning module that performs iterative, interpretable inference over object-centric 3D features.
Explicitly model spatial and relational priors (e.g., via graph-based reasoning or attention over object relations) to disambiguate referents using multi-step logic.
Use reasoning-aware training objectives and targeted supervision or prompts that encourage stepwise decomposition of complex referring expressions.
impact: Makes 3D grounding more accurate and robust for real-world tasks—helpful for robotics, AR/VR, and multimodal applications where precise language-to-3D mapping and relational understanding are critical.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: 3D encoder + text encoder → reasoning module (iterative steps) → predicted referent
Before/after scene examples: challenging queries where baseline fails but reasoning-enabled model succeeds
Object-relation graph or attention heatmap showing multi-step inference and which relations were used
Bar/line chart: performance gains across categories (relational, compositional, occluded) compared to baselines
paper_authors: Hsiang-Wei Huang, Kuang-Ming Chen, Wenhao Chai, Cheng-Yen Yang, Jen-Hao Cheng
